title: Sample: Eng standup

segments.speaker: Me
segments.text: Morning, everyone. Let's keep it quick today, I've got a hard stop at quarter to.

segments.speaker: Me
segments.text: Maya, do you want to kick us off?

segments.speaker: Maya
segments.text: Sure. So yesterday I mostly watched the Fernhollow dashboards after the dedupe fix went out on Tuesday.

segments.speaker: Maya
segments.text: Zero new duplicates in two days, and Owen confirmed the same on his side this morning. So I'm calling the incident closed.

segments.speaker: Me
segments.text: Nice. That's a big one. Thank you.

segments.speaker: Maya
segments.text: Today I'm back on Calendar Sync v2, writing the subscription renewal part of the design doc. No blockers. And, uh, first morning off the pager, which is lovely.

segments.speaker: Me
segments.text: Well earned. Okay, Diego, you're up.

segments.speaker: Diego
segments.text: Yeah. Yesterday I got the read-only offline job list caching working on Android. Today I'm starting the iOS side.

segments.speaker: Diego
segments.text: I am kind of blocked, though. I need a last modified at field on each job in the jobs list endpoint, so the app knows when its cached copy is stale.

segments.speaker: Diego
segments.text: Right now I'm diffing the whole payload, which works, but it's slow and it's going to be terrible on a bad connection out in somebody's basement.

segments.speaker: Maya
segments.text: Oh, that one's on me, sorry. I said I'd add it last week and then the incident ate the week.

segments.speaker: Maya
segments.text: It's a small change. I can have it on the endpoint by end of day tomorrow.

segments.speaker: Diego
segments.text: Tomorrow works. I'll stub it on my side until then.

segments.speaker: Diego
segments.text: For context, the Android cache keeps the next fourteen days of jobs for the technician, so it's usually under two hundred jobs. It loads in about a second from cold.

segments.speaker: Diego
segments.text: On iOS I'm reusing the same cache schema, so hopefully it's two or three days of work, not a week.

segments.speaker: Me
segments.text: Two or three days is fine. Nothing's waiting on it this week.

segments.speaker: Me
segments.text: Does that mean the offline list misses today's cut?

segments.speaker: Diego
segments.text: Yeah. Honestly it was never really going to make this one. I'd rather it goes out in next week's release with the real field than hack around it.

segments.speaker: Me
segments.text: Okay, agreed. Offline list goes in next week's release, not this one. Priya?

segments.speaker: Priya
segments.text: Yesterday was mostly SOC 2 prep. Kestrel Audit sent over their evidence request list, it's about sixty items, and I've mapped maybe two thirds of them to things we already collect.

segments.speaker: Priya
segments.text: Kestrel wants the observation window to start cleanly on the first of November, so everything on that list needs an owner by the end of next week.

segments.speaker: Priya
segments.text: I'll send each of you the handful of items that are yours on Monday. Most of it is screenshots of settings, nothing scary.

segments.speaker: Me
segments.text: Is anything on there going to surprise us?

segments.speaker: Priya
segments.text: Access reviews for the production database, probably. We've never done a formal one. I'll draft a process, but that's a next-week problem.

segments.speaker: Priya
segments.text: The other thing is the flaky test. The webhook retry integration test has failed something like one in eight runs this week, always on the timeout assertion.

segments.speaker: Priya
segments.text: I'm quarantining it this morning so it stops blocking merges, and I'll file a ticket with the logs I've got so far.

segments.speaker: Me
segments.text: Is it a real bug or just the test?

segments.speaker: Priya
segments.text: I think it's the test. It sleeps for a fixed two seconds and then checks the retry fired, and the CI runners are just slower some days. But I want to look properly before I say that for sure.

segments.speaker: Maya
segments.text: It does touch the retry queue I'm about to rewrite for v2, so I'm happy to pair on it next week if it turns out to be real.

segments.speaker: Priya
segments.text: Maybe. Let's see what the logs say first.

segments.speaker: Priya
segments.text: And today I'm driving the release cut. Plan's still Thursday afternoon, so four o'clock today. If you've got something that needs to be in, merge it by three thirty.

segments.speaker: Me
segments.text: And the quarantined test won't block the cut?

segments.speaker: Priya
segments.text: No, quarantined tests still run but they don't gate anything. No blockers from me.

segments.speaker: Me
segments.text: Great, thanks, everyone. That's us for today.

notes:
> This is a sample meeting, so you can see what Deino writes after a call. Delete it whenever you like.

### Updates
- **Maya:** closed the Fernhollow duplicates incident, with no new duplicates in two days. Back on Calendar Sync v2, writing the subscription renewal design.
- **Diego:** offline job list caching works on Android; starting iOS with the same cache schema (two or three days).
- **Priya:** SOC 2 prep with Kestrel Audit. About 60 evidence items, two thirds already mapped. Driving today's release cut.

### Decisions
- The offline job list ships in next week's release, not today's cut.
- The flaky webhook retry test is quarantined, so it stops blocking merges.

### Blockers and risks
- Diego needs a last-modified field on the jobs list endpoint to detect stale caches.
- Production database access reviews have never been done formally.

### Next
- Release cut at 4 pm. Merge anything that needs to be in by 3:30.
